why: The doc sentence is verbatim (goal.md:106, whole line: '`stop`, `off`, `reset`, `none`, and `cancel` are accepted as aliases for `clear`. Running `/clear` to start a new conversation also removes any active goal.' - the second sentence does not reverse it), and all three cited file:lines say what was claimed (slash-command-menu.tsx:17 has no `goal` member; harness-tool-descriptor.ts:286 is `sessionBinding('goal', 'Goal')`; goal-service.ts:31-38 is `GoalCommand`). But the load-bearing assertion built on them - '`GoalCommand` is reachable only through the `mcp__session__Goal` tool binding', hence 'a user cannot set, inspect or clear a goal' - is false. There is a second, explicitly USER-sourced path that is not model-invocable at all: `PiHarnessRuntimeControlRequestV1` carries `goal_create`, `goal_replace`, `goal_cancel`, `goal_complete`, `goal_blocked` and `goal_resume` (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:346-351); they are validated in packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:295-328 (which also REJECTS a caller-supplied `source`, see its test at :65) and handled in packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3279-3324, where `goal_create`/`goal_replace` call `GoalService.execute` with `source: 'user', creator: 'desktop'` and then `schedulePiGoalContinuation`. That surface is wired the whole way out: RPC `sessions.ts:246` -> preload `apps/electron/src/preload/bootstrap.ts:214` (`controlPiHarnessRuntime`) -> renderer hook `apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useAgentPanel.ts:121-123` (`control`), already held by ChatDisplay.tsx:717. Inspection is wired too: `PiHarnessRuntimeSnapshotV1.goal` (pi-harness-runtime.ts:308) carries condition, status, budgets, accounting and `lastEvaluation.reason` - the exact data Claude's no-arg `/goal` status shows - and it is parsed for the renderer in packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts. So a user-set, user-cleared goal is a first-class modelled concept here, not an agent-only one, and the goal loop itself (settlement evaluator via `runMiniCompletion`, continuation dispatch, budgets) is implemented at SessionManager.ts:3360-3400. This is exactly the repo's recurring false-positive shape: the identifier is genuinely absent, but the consequence is wrong because a sibling path already handles it. Secondary: the parity audit already records `/goal` as a *completion condition* under section 5's 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness' list (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1722), so it is a triaged item, not an unnoticed gap. (It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 - `goal` does not appear in that file at all - so I do not claim owner-decision cover.)
correctedState: Nessy implements the goal loop (condition, per-turn settlement evaluation through the mini model, automatic continuation dispatch, plus turn/token/cost/elapsed budgets and evidence-backed complete/blocked states that Claude's /goal does not have; condition cap 8192 chars vs Claude's 4000). It is reachable BOTH by the model, through `sessionBinding('goal', 'Goal')` with `source` forced to 'agent'/'pi' (SessionManager.ts:12148-12155), AND by the user, through the `goal_create`/`goal_replace`/`goal_cancel`/`goal_complete`/`goal_blocked`/`goal_resume` runtime-control actions that set `source: 'user', creator: 'desktop'` (pi-harness-runtime.ts:346-351; SessionManager.ts:3279-3324), exposed over RPC, preload and the `useAgentPanel` hook the chat view already holds; the goal summary is delivered to the renderer on every runtime snapshot. What is actually missing is only the last-mile affordance and Claude's exact command grammar: no `goal` member in the built-in `SlashCommandId` union (slash-command-menu.tsx:17), no rendered goal indicator or control in the agent panel (ChatDisplay.tsx:2330-2336 renders child rows only, though `chat.piRuntime.goal` and `chat.piAgentView.goal` labels already exist in every locale), no no-arg status view, and no `clear`/`stop`/`off`/`reset`/`none`/`cancel` alias parsing - our cancel is an id+revision optimistic-concurrency call rather than a bare word. So the gap is a UI/command-grammar gap on top of an implemented, user-addressable service, not 'the goal is model-only'.
